items.title: Arthur "Monk" Hazel Interview, 1959-07-16
items.q: And I went to Leon Primer's house and got Leon with it, was 16 at the time.

ctx.x: He didn't touch the horn. He gave me the horn. That's how I come and start playing the corner. When he, when he, when he, he gave me, yeah, well we, uh, it was his, uh, it was his, uh, 21st birthday. And in, in the meantime, uh, uh, the Eckert band had, had split up. Uh, half of the band went with Tony Forgerat. And, uh, and the other half of the band I had, uh, the original piano player and a kid by the name of Elroy Mazur on saxophone. And I went to Leon Primer's house and got Leon with it, was 16 at the time.…
Was that well known as a musician or as a musician?

items.title: Arthur "Monk" Hazel Interview, 1967-10-28
items.q: And I played it, the clarinet, you know, with the drums, Leon would, Leon would just play the show.

ctx.x: And, uh, uh, and I was working at the 500 Club then. Leon Prima had the 500 Club then. That was before their revival, you know. Yes. You had to, you had to really scuffle around and start to try to hear any jazz. As a matter of fact, for a good while, we had, you know, we were playing the only jazz in New Orleans, because the rest of the bands would either go on Latin or go on arrangements and things that you couldn't hear in the real jazz. Yeah, those were tough days for traditional music, weren't they? And we…

Well, Monk, we want to get back to this. I want to have you back again in a week or so, so that we can play some of your older records, which I couldn't get a hold of right now. But let's take a short break here, and then we'll come back with some more modern music that I want you to kind of evaluate for us, if you would. We'll be right back after this message.
